scope: Only CPU-per-GPU thresholds and the 98%-free versus PyTorch allocated-plus-reserved<=2% diagnostic definition. All host MDX source files were searched; no non-host corpus scan, execution or live call.

matching_occurrences.text: - At least one physical CPU core per visible/listed GPU. Hyperthreads do not count.
| CPU | AVX-capable, with at least one physical core per listed GPU. |

Before installing, make sure the host has supported same-type GPUs, native Ubuntu/Linux, an AVX-capable CPU, at least one physical CPU core per listed GPU, adequate RAM, fast SSD/NVMe storage, working compatible GPU drivers, stable public networking, and enough direct ports forwarded for both TCP and UDP.
For CPU capacity, use the physical-core rule: the host should have at least one visible physical CPU core per visible GPU. Hyperthreads and logical CPUs do not count as physical cores.

| `cpu.cores`
CPU cores | Required: `offer.cpu_cores` >= 2 × `num_gpus` | The CLI checks the reported offer core count against twice the listed GPU count. This check does not establish how `offer.cpu_cores` was measured. | Check the reported core count and GPU count; add CPU capacity or reduce the listed GPU count if this preflight gate is unmet. |

| `system_requirements`
System requirements | For each visible GPU, PyTorch allocated plus reserved memory must be at most 2% of its reported VRAM; system RAM is at least 95% of total GPU VRAM capped at 2,000,000 MiB; there are at least 2 physical CPU cores per visible GPU, counted with `psutil.cpu_count(logical=False)`. Hyperthreads/logical CPUs do not count as physical cores. | Verify GPU visibility, available VRAM, host RAM, and CPU core capacity. | Check CUDA visibility, host memory, CPU allocation, and competing GPU workloads. |
- Each GPU has at least 98% free VRAM.
- At least one visible physical CPU core per visible GPU.
